summary: Home's files, whole. A file of your home opens in its program through A1's door (appfile.open takes Files or Home; its save recorded through L4's revisions.record, which now records files of Files or of your home, never elsewhere); the working view's watcher records a Home file's revisions too, and a Home file focused on the board is watched (another program's save recorded, a rename found by inode). The Files tree gets the owner's own actions on files and folders of Home (and of Files where it lives in Home): right-click Open in <program>, Rename..., Move to..., New folder..., Delete, Open here, Open with, Copy the path; drag a row onto a folder of the tree to move it (or onto DELETE); a line under the tab's header says what was done, with Undo (old name, old folder, restore, a new folder into DELETE). Delete of a Home file goes to the system's own bin, the freedesktop.org Trash in ~/.local/share/Trash (new workbench/home_trash.py: .trashinfo with Path and DeletionDate written first and claimed exclusively, then one rename; another drive refused; restore puts it back, beside it under a free name when taken), through the same files.trash / files.trash_list / files.restore operations (no new operation, registry unchanged). The DELETE room lists 'From your home' with restore; the DELETE count includes it. Her changes pass home_reach.her_change first: files (may_change, as L6), K2 (L6), A1 (appfile.open in her work), K5 (office_bridge._file on edit, Home documents by whole path), K9 (a11y_hand._resolve), K6 (Apply as L6; inputs may be read from Home). On screen the place is always DELETE (the owner's word, and test_delete_words): the menu row is 'Delete', not 'Delete to Trash'.

decisions: On screen the place is DELETE everywhere (the owner's word of 14 Nov, held by tests_integrated/test_delete_words.py: no 'Trash' string constant in workbench/*.py): the menu row is 'Delete' (key trash), the Undo line says 'is in DELETE', the room's section is 'From your home'; the plan's and the coordinator's 'Delete to Trash' wording was not used. The bin's real folder (~/.local/share/Trash) is shown only as a path computed at run time in the room's lead; the specification's words ([Trash Info], the folder name) are bytes constants.

No new Kernel operation: files.trash of a path in your home (outside Files and Graphite's own) goes to the freedesktop Trash, kept in files_trash as stored "~trash:<name>" so story and Undo find it; files.trash_list adds "home" (every entry of the home bin, other programs' too, each with the id files.restore takes) and "home_trash"; files.restore restores those ids first. tools/record_registry.py --check on the copy: no differences, so docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json was not regenerated.

files.trash refuses your home folder itself and any folder that is or holds Graphite's workspace, its Files or its program (FILES_RESERVED); the tree offers no rename, move or Delete for those. Before this, files.trash of the home folder was stopped only by shutil ("into itself").

A path outside your home and outside Files keeps L6's behaviour on files.trash (into Files' DELETE); the home bin is for the home. A thing in your home on another drive than the bin is refused with words, nothing moved (no copy-then-remove); per-drive bins ($topdir/.Trash-$uid) are not built.

Revisions (L4) and A1's door accept a file of Files or of your home; anywhere else revisions.record/appfile.open say REVISIONS_OUTSIDE / APPFILE_OUTSIDE before any id is made. A1 keeps a Home file's session and watched files by its whole path.

A focused Home file (not Files: L1 watches Files) is watched with a QFileSystemWatcher on the file and its folder; another program's save is recorded through revisions.record as "outside" unless an A1 session or an open working view of it records it with its own words; a rename in its folder is found by inode and keeps its id.
Undo of New folder puts the folder in DELETE (never rmdir); restore when the name is taken puts it beside under "name 2.ext".
The menu provider for Home rows runs before S2's, so the first row is A1's "Open in <program>"; S2's Open with stays under More.

K5 accepts a document of your home (kept by its whole path) with her_change on every edit; K9's _resolve passes her_change for every act (her hand works only on Files or your home); K6's inputs may be read from your home (Apply keeps L6's her_change).
The DELETE room's Files lead reads "Nothing from Files is in DELETE." when only things from your home are there (set from home_files_qt.trash_rows, no wider edit of files_qt).

release_note: Home's files, whole: in the Files tree a file or folder of your home can be opened in its program (its saves recorded as revisions), renamed, moved (also by dragging it onto a folder), given a new folder beside it, and deleted, each with Undo. Deleting a file of your home puts it in DELETE through the system's own bin (~/.local/share/Trash, shared with your other programs), with where it was and when; DELETE lists it under 'From your home' and restore puts it back, never over another file. A file of your home in focus or open is watched: a save by another program is noticed and recorded. Kasandra's changes still reach only inside your home, under your grants.
